props.title: Constantine

sections.content: Constantine (2005) marked a pivotal moment in occult noir cinema, blending Catholic mythology with hardboiled detective elements. Keanu Reeves portrays John Constantine as a chain-smoking exorcist caught between Heaven and Hell, channeling the cynical edge of Hellblazer comics while establishing its own visual language. The film shares DNA with The Crow (1994) and Blade (1998) in its gothic urban aesthetic, but director Francis Lawrence pushes further into religious horror territory. The film's depiction of Hell as a nuclear-scorched Los Angeles creates an unforgettable parallel dimension that influenced supernatural thrillers like Legion (2010) and Priest (2011).

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond its religious horror elements. Its stylized action sequences, particularly the holy water brass knuckles and mirror realm battles, created a template for supernatural combat that echoes through films like Doctor Strange (2016) and The Last Witch Hunter (2015). The film's depiction of angels and demons as corporate bureaucrats fighting a cold war influenced later works like Good Omens (2019) and Supernatural (2005-2020), showing how celestial politics could be both terrifying and darkly humorous. SUBHEAD: Religious Horror Evolution

Constantine bridges classic religious horror like The Exorcist (1973) with modern urban fantasy. Its approach to demonology and exorcism influenced films like Deliver Us from Evil (2014) and The Rite (2011), while its noir elements echo through Dylan Dog: Dead of Night (2011) and R.I.P.D. (2013). The film's visual effects team created groundbreaking demon designs that still hold up, particularly the water mirror sequence and Tilda Swinton's androgynous angel Gabriel.
